overview: This paper establishes minimax lower bounds on the sample complexity of ReLU message-passing GNNs—Ω(√(log d/n)) for inductive graph-level prediction and Ω(d/log n) for transductive node-level prediction under spectral-homophily conditions—and empirically validates these rates through ratio-based scaling diagnostics on synthetic worst-case/bottleneck graphs and real benchmarks (ogbn_arxiv, ogbn_products_50k, Reddit_50k) using GCN, GAT, and GraphSAGE architectures.

modules.name: Spectral Analysis and Structural Diagnostics
modules.description: Compute the normalized Laplacian of a graph, extract its second-smallest eigenvalue λ₂(L), calculate the spectral gap, compute label homophily scores over edges, and certify the spectral–homophily condition λ₂(L) ≤ κ₀/log n across a training-size grid by determining the dataset-level constant κ₀.

modules.name: Synthetic Worst-Case Graph Construction (Theorem 1)
modules.description: Construct path (chain) graphs that instantiate the worst-case regime of Theorem 1. Generate node features from isotropic Gaussians, produce labels via the packing-constructed ReLU GNN subclass with Varshamov-Gilbert codeword-based first-layer weights, and add Gaussian noise to labels. This module directly instantiates the minimax error curve √(log d/n).

modules.name: Synthetic Bottleneck Graph Construction (Theorem 2)
modules.description: Build an SBM-like undirected graph with K communities and controlled bottleneck structure (pin ≫ pout) satisfying the spectral–homophily condition. Generate d-dimensional Gaussian node features, produce labels via a teacher model combining a global linear projection with community-dependent bias and quantile binning into discrete classes, and record spectral and homophily diagnostics for certification.

modules.name: Large-Scale Benchmark Subsampling Pipeline
modules.description: Extract 50k-node induced subgraphs from ogbn-products and Reddit by drawing a 200k random candidate set, computing the largest connected component, and uniformly sampling exactly 50k nodes while preserving OGB-style train/val/test split mappings. Save the node-index mapping for deterministic reproducibility.

modules.name: GNN Architecture Implementations
modules.description: Implement the three evaluated architectures—2-layer GCN with GCNConv, 2-layer GAT with multi-head attention in the first layer and single head in the second, and 2-layer GraphSAGE with SAGEConv—all using ReLU activation after the first layer and configurable hidden dimensions. The implementations must integrate with PyTorch Geometric and support both node classification and graph regression output heads.

modules.name: Sample-Size Grid Training Pipeline
modules.description: Execute the main training loop over a log-spaced grid of training sizes n, for each n randomly subsampling the labeled node set, training the GNN with Adam optimizer and early stopping on validation loss, and repeating across multiple random seeds. Aggregate per-seed test losses and accuracies, computing means, standard deviations, and 95% confidence intervals.

modules.name: Packing Set and Varshamov-Gilbert Code Construction
modules.description: Implement the combinatorial packing construction underlying both theorems: generate constant-weight binary codes over {0,1}^d with minimum Hamming distance d/8 and cardinality ≥ 2^{d/8} via the Varshamov-Gilbert bound. Build the ReLU GNN packing set {f_S} indexed by subsets S of coordinates, compute L2(PX) separations under Gaussian features, and verify the packing number lower bound log M ≥ C_A v_s^2 log(d) / (L^2 ε^2).

modules.name: Fano's Inequality and KL Divergence Computation
modules.description: Implement the fixed-radius form of Fano's inequality (Lemma 1) and the Gaussian regression KL divergence formula. Given a packing set with known pairwise L2 separations and noise variance σ², compute the maximum pairwise KL divergence, apply Fano's bound to obtain the minimax risk lower bound as a function of ε², and optimize over ε² (solving the resulting quadratic) to extract the tight rate.

modules.name: Minimax Risk Estimation for Both Theorems
modules.description: Combine the packing construction, KL control, and Fano optimization into end-to-end procedures yielding the theoretical lower bounds: (1) Theorem 1's Ω(σv_s/L · √(log d/n)) for the inductive setting on path graphs, and (2) Theorem 2's Ω(σ²v_s²/(ΓL²) · d/log n) for the transductive setting under spectral–homophily, including the block-count argument that reduces effective sample size to K = ⌈c_blk log n⌉.

modules.name: Ratio-Based Scaling Diagnostics
modules.description: Compute the primary empirical diagnostics: Ratio1(n) = Err(n)/√(log d/n) aligned with Theorem 1 and Ratio2(n) = Err(n)/(d/log n) aligned with Theorem 2. Evaluate ratio stability across n by tracking trends and fitting slopes. A stable (flat) ratio indicates empirical consistency with the corresponding theoretical rate; a steadily increasing ratio indicates inconsistency. Also estimate the empirical constant C⋆ as the plateau value of the preferred ratio.

modules.name: Scaling Law Curve Fitting
modules.description: Fit four candidate asymptotic models to the mean test loss vs. n curves using weighted nonlinear least squares with inverse-variance weights: c₁ + α/√n, c₂ + β/n, c₃ + δ/log n, and c₄ + 1/n^γ. Compute weighted RSS, MSE, and R² for each fit, select the best-fit model by maximum R², and report fitted parameters and fit quality metrics. Treat this as secondary (supporting) evidence subordinate to the ratio diagnostics.

modules.name: Operator-Norm Control for Attention Architectures
modules.description: Implement the operator-norm analysis for adjacency-masked attention layers (Appendices I–J) that extends Theorem 2 to GAT. Compute per-layer Lipschitz constants for masked attention by bounding softmax row-stochastic matrices under adjacency masking, controlling attention logits via temperature/clipping, and verifying that the product of layer norms yields a uniform bound. This validates that the Ω(d/log n) rate applies to GAT under the stated norm constraints.

modules.name: Result Aggregation, Visualization, and Report Generation
modules.description: Aggregate all experimental outputs—raw error tables with mean±std across seeds, ratio diagnostic plots (Ratio1 and Ratio2 vs. n for each dataset-model pair), curve-fit overlays, structural diagnostic tables (λ₂, κ₀, homophily), and comparison tables of fit metrics (RSS, MSE, R², best-fit model). Generate publication-quality figures with error bars and LaTeX-formatted tables.

modules.name: Configuration Management and Experiment Tracking
modules.description: Manage experiment configurations (dataset selection, model architecture hyperparameters, training-size grids, seed counts, optimizer settings) via structured configs. Track all random seeds for deterministic reproducibility, log training progress and intermediate results, persist model checkpoints with early-stopping state, and coordinate the full pipeline from data loading through structural verification, training, diagnostics, and report generation.
